title: Intrinsic affine self-Tor coordinates compatible with one canonical quotient lift
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. Use the standard derived category [def-pc-derived-category] and the fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Put B=i_*O_Z, D=Q(B[0]), and Q_n=H^{-n}(D tensor-derived D), for n≥0. On each affine U put A_U=Gamma(Y,U), I_U=ker(i)(U), P_U the chosen projective resolution of A_U/I_U, and T_U=P_U tensor A_U/I_U [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. There exist A_U-linear equivalences c_U:H_n(T_U)≃Gamma(U,Q_n). For each basic inclusion V⊆U, let phi be ring restriction and psi the canonical Ideal.quotientMap, using ideal restriction. There exist one augmented chain map a:P_U→Res_phi(P_V) and one tensor chain map k:T_U→Res_phi(T_V), with pi_V(a_0(x))=psi(pi_U(x)) and k_j(x tensor y)=a_j(x) tensor psi(y), such that restriction(c_U(x))=c_V(e(H_n(k)(x))) for every x. Here e is exact restriction-of-scalars homology comparison. This asserts existence of a compatible lift, not compatibility with every supplied lift.

source.place: Tag 08DX(2), affine derived tensor construction; Tags 06YH, 01I9(2) and 00LS(1), normalized coefficient sheaf, derived tensor, and existence of augmented resolution lifts.

proof.text: For every affine U use i.ker_apply and i.app_surjective to form the canonical quotient section linear equivalence s_U: A_U/I_U -> Gamma(U,i_*O_Z), normalized by s_U(mk x)=i.app U x. RingHom.lift_injective_of_ker_le_ideal and Ideal.Quotient.lift_surjective_of_surjective prove bijectivity, and map_mul proves A_U-linearity. The proved source Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isClosedImmersion applied to the quasi-coherent unit proves B is quasi-coherent. These are direct applications of the existing ring quotient and closed-immersion APIs, with no new geometric assumption.

Take a global K-flat resolution q:K -> B[0]. Apply the natural K-flat derived tensor comparison to constant singleton families K and B[0]. Q(q) is invertible. Tensor its inverse with the identity and compose with the comparison to obtain D tensor D -> Q(Tot(K tensor B[0])). Apply degree -n homology and homologyFunctorFactors, and invert to obtain a global sheaf isomorphism e from ordinary tensor homology to intrinsic self-Tor.

Apply the ordinary quasi-coherent tensor-resolution coordinate theorem to B,B, the normalized quotient section coordinates s,s, and the chosen algebraic projective resolutions. Compose its c_U with the linear equivalence on sections of the global e. For every basic inclusion construct psi0,a,k using the proved quotient-resolution tensor comparison. Quotient surjectivity and the formula on mk identify psi0 with the required Ideal.quotientMap.

Regard the canonical quotient homomorphism as the semilinear coefficient map b. Reduce its coordinate restriction equation to representatives mk x by quotient surjectivity; s_U(mk x)=i.app U x and i.naturality give exactly the required equation. The augmentation equation for a then gives the first-coefficient restriction equation. Apply the ordinary coordinate naturality to b,a,k and these equations. Finally PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply e.hom transports this equality to intrinsic self-Tor. This last assembly is explicitly proved in Lean and uses no new hole.

proof_origin.place: K-flat representative computation (2), with ordinary affine comparison separated from derived localization and quotient augmentation construction; canonical quotient normalization proved from Mathlib.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derived_selfTor_chosen_affine_coordinates
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℕ) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := CochainComplex.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let D := DerivedCategory.Q.obj (S.obj B)
    let Q := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (-(n : ℤ))).obj (D ⊗ D)
    ∃ c : ∀ U : Y.affineOpens,
        ((((tensorRight (ModuleCat.of (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
          ((Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) ⧸ i.ker.ideal U))).mapHomologicalComplex (.down ℕ)).obj
            (projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
              ((Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) ⧸ i.ker.ideal U))).complex).homology n) ≃ₗ[Γ(Y, U.1)]
              Q.val.obj (op U.1),
      ∀ (V U : Y.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ U.1)
        (_hbasic : ∃ f : Γ(Y, U.1), Y.basicOpen f = V.1),
          let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
          let C := (Γ(Y, V.1) : Type u)
          let I := i.ker.ideal U
          let J := i.ker.ideal V
          let φ := (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
          let P := projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))
          let R := projectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))
          let TA := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)
          let TC := (tensorRight (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ J))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.down ℕ)
          let ψ := Ideal.quotientMap J φ
            (fun x hx ↦ i.ker.ideal_le_comap_ideal h hx)
          ∃ (a : P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.down ℕ)).obj R.complex)
            (k : TA.obj P.complex ⟶ ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.down ℕ)).obj (TC.obj R.complex)),
            (∀ x : P.complex.X 0, R.π.f 0 (a.f 0 x) = ψ (P.π.f 0 x)) ∧
            (∀ (j : ℕ) (x : P.complex.X j) (y : A ⧸ I),
              k.f j (x ⊗ₜ[A] y) = (show R.complex.X j from a.f j x) ⊗ₜ[C] (ψ y)) ∧
            let e := ((TC.obj R.complex).sc n).mapHomologyIso
              (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ)
          ∀ x, Q.val.map (homOfLE h).op (c U x) =
            c V (e.hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap k n x))
